memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They made crossbars of acacia wood: five for the frames on one side of the tabernacle, five for those on the other side, and five for the frames on the west, at the far end of the tabernacle. They made the centre crossbar so that it extended from end to end at the middle of the frames." - Exod 36:31-33 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The frames stood upright, but they still needed to be tied together. So crossbars ran horizontally through them — and one long centre bar ran the entire length, from end to end.

Vertical strength was not enough. Something had to run through everything and connect it all.

This is a helpful picture for our lives. We can have good individual habits — prayer here, church there, honesty at work, patience at home — and still live in compartments, with no single thread running through. God is not meant to be one section of life. He is meant to be the centre bar running end to end.

Paul prays that Christ may dwell in our hearts through faith, and that we might be rooted and established in love (Eph 3:17). Not visited. Dwelling. Running through.

Ask where the disconnects are. Is the person you are on Sunday recognisable on Wednesday afternoon? Does the way you speak about people match the way you pray for them?

And notice the crossbars were hidden, running through the middle of the frames. What holds your life together should be so deeply integrated that people see the effect without seeing the mechanism.

One life, one Lord, end to end.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is your life integrated, or divided into compartments?
2. Where is the biggest gap between your Sunday self and your weekday self?
3. What would it look like for Christ to run "end to end" through your week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, run through every part of my life. Let there be no compartment where You are not welcome. Amen.
